scope: Every environment variable read by the scanned roots, with its readers, scope, secret grade and template declaration. Generated; do not edit by hand.

safety.codeLiteralsIncluded: Fallback and comparison literals are copied from source code, which is already public in the repository; email addresses are replaced with <email address>.

tiers.app: read by app/, lib/, components/, middleware.ts or instrumentation.ts
tiers.build: read by next.config.mjs or capacitor.config.ts at build time
tiers.mobile: read by the Expo app under mobile/src (EXPO_PUBLIC_* values are inlined at build)
tiers.operator-scripts: read by scripts/ that a person runs by hand (and possibly by tests), and not bound by any workflow
tiers.ci-scripts: read by scripts/ and also bound by a .github/workflows env: block or read by a scripts/ci-*.mjs file: CI plumbing an operator may also set
tiers.ci-only: bound only by a .github/workflows env: block (and possibly read by tests)
tiers.tests-only: read only by tests/ or the test-runner configs
tiers.set-but-never-read: only set by tests (process.env.X = …, vi.stubEnv) or only declared in a template; no scanned code reads it

rules.templateRule: Every variable in the app, build, mobile or operator-scripts tier is declared exactly once in .env.example or mobile/.env.example, unless the platform supplies it. Tests-only and CI-only variables are listed here and need no template line; the few a developer sets by hand to run the e2e suite locally are also in the test-only block of .env.example.
rules.secret: Secret-grade when the name matches /(SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|PRIVATE_KEY|API_KEY|SERVICE_ROLE_KEY|_DB_URL$|^GOOGLE_SEARCH_CONSOLE_KEY$|^SYNC_TOKEN_KEY$)/ (except NEXT_PUBLIC_*/EXPO_PUBLIC_* and file-path names), or when a read is passed to configuredSecret/secretEquals/timingSafeEqual/createHmac/safeEqual. A workflow binding from secrets.* is recorded (boundFromWorkflowSecret) but does not by itself make a name secret-grade: CI also stores public keys and project refs as secrets. A secret-grade name in .env.example carries a [secret] tag in its comment.
rules.reads: process.env.X, process.env["X"], const { X } = process.env, an alias initialised from process.env (or a parameter named env indexed by a computed key) read as alias.X, string literals listed in a file that indexes process.env by a computed key (e.g. credentialEnv in lib/social/capabilities.ts), and env: bindings in workflows. Assignments, delete and vi.stubEnv count as sets, not reads. Comments and strings never count.
rules.facts: fallback-literal / fallback-variable / fallback-expression: what follows ?? or || at the read. compared-with: a literal the value is compared with. passed-to: the call the value is handed to. validated-by-regex: a regex .test() on the variable the value is stored in, within the same function.
rules.notScanned: Shell, Python and SQL files; mobile/app.json extra (a fallback for EXPO_PUBLIC_*); vercel.json; Supabase config.

The Alexa skill's application id, from the Alexa developer console (amzn1.ask.skill.<uuid>). /api/assistant/alexa always verifies Amazon's request signature; this additionally pins the requests to OUR skill. Amazon signs any skill's requests, so without it somebody else's skill could name our endpoint and its signature would be genuine. Leave blank only before the skill exists — the setup docs and the Assistants page both say to set it.

Leave this UNSET everywhere except a local machine. Every Twilio-facing webhook (Guardian inbound SMS/voice/WhatsApp, screening, voicemail status, escalation TwiML, and the Contact Center's voice and SMS callbacks) is on the middleware PUBLIC allowlist: the caller is Twilio, not a signed-in person, so the request signature is the only thing standing between those endpoints and anyone at all. lib/server/twilio-ingress.ts therefore verifies on every request, in every environment, and refuses with 503 when TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN is absent and it cannot verify at all. Unsigned fixtures require NODE_ENV=test and this flag set to 1, with TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN unset. A configured token always requires a valid signature. Production, development and unset modes refuse unverifiable callbacks even if this fixture flag is copied into their environment.
